problem_summary.summary: Check whether two strings contain exactly the same characters with the same multiplicities.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: lowercase English strings s and t. Return true if t is a rearrangement of s, otherwise false.
constraints: Both strings contain lowercase English letters

brute_force.explanation: Convert both strings to character arrays, sort them, and compare the sorted arrays.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Sorting places each character in a canonical position determined by its value. The sorted arrays match exactly iff the original strings had identical character counts.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n log n), where n is the common string length.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(n) auxiliary for the two character arrays.

optimized.explanation: Count each letter from s in a 26-entry array and subtract each letter from t. Equal lengths are required, and no counter may become negative.
optimized.correctness_idea: A final zero count for every letter means the strings contain exactly the same multiplicities. A negative count means t uses a letter more often than s.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n), one pass over both strings plus a fixed 26-entry check.
optimized.space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary: the frequency array has fixed size.
